battle.name: 迪亞烏希-亞述戰爭
battle.theater: 敘利亞北部奧龍特斯河中游
battle.brief: 公元前十二世紀末，亞述在西進途中與埃及的遠征部隊在「迪亞烏希」相遇，戰地位置至今未經考定。敘事文本記兩軍在城外列陣：埃及步兵以持矛為主，長矛列於前列，弓手在後成排射擊；亞述則以鐵刃長矛、密集弓箭與騎兵配合車隊衝鋒。此役不見於任何一方的官方碑刻，勝敗無從確證。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 迪亞烏希-亞述戰爭是公元前十二世紀末埃及與亞述之間的一場交鋒。戰地「迪亞烏希」（Dia-uš）只在楔形文字的敘事文本裡留下名字，位置至今未經考古確認，因此戰場只能作大致標定。埃及一方是第二中間期向第三中間期過渡時期的王室軍隊：此時法老的權威已大不如新王國時代，實權分散在三角洲的坦尼斯系王室與上游的亞蒙神最高祭司之間，軍隊規模與訓練都大幅下滑，靠三角洲的農業剩餘維持一支以僱傭兵為主的部隊，並倚賴努比亞與地中海東岸的弓手。亞述一方是中亞述王國，王表上這一段可考的君主有 Apil-Eshin、Ashur-bel-kala 及其子 Tiglat-Pileser I（約前1114–前1076年在位）；此時亞述剛在西邊站穩腳跟，正把勢力伸進阿馬爾（Amurru）與幼發拉底中上游。埃及與亞述的直接交涉在十四世紀的阿馬爾納書信中留有大量文字，之後便是近一個世紀的空白；迪亞烏希是這段空白之後兩國最接近的一次碰撞。雙方的指揮系統都極簡：埃及是法老加地方首領，亞述是國王加省級總督加軍官，命令靠縱隊內的口信與鼓號傳遞，陣地一旦拉開就難以協調，戰役因此常常在幾個時辰內決定。
countriesEn: The Battle of Dium Ush was a clash between Egypt and Assyria in the late twelfth century BC. The site called Dium Ush survives only as a name in a cuneiform narrative text, and it has never been confirmed archaeologically, so the battlefield can be fixed only roughly. On the Egyptian side stood the royal forces of Egypt in the transition from the Second Intermediate Period to the Third Intermediate Period. The authority of the pharaoh was by then far below what it had been in the New Kingdom, and effective power was divided between the Tanite line of kings in the Delta and the High Priests of Amun upriver; the army was smaller and less well trained than in the New Kingdom, sustained by the agricultural surplus of the Delta and centred on mercenaries, with Nubian archers and archers from the eastern Mediterranean in its ranks. On the Assyrian side stood the Middle Assyrian kingdom. The rulers whose reigns can be aligned with this stretch of the Middle Assyrian king list are Apil-Eshin, Ashur-bel-kala and his son Tiglat-Pileser I, who reigned about 1114 to 1076 BC; Assyria had just secured a foothold in the west and was extending its reach into the Amurru and the middle Euphrates. Direct dealings between Egypt and Assyria are abundantly attested in the Amarna correspondence of the fourteenth century, and then there follows a gap of close to a century. Dium Ush is the closest the two countries came to collision in that gap. The command structures on both sides were minimal: for Egypt, a pharaoh with local dynasts; for Assyria, a king with provincial governors and officers, orders carried by word of mouth and by horn and drum signals inside the column, so that once the formations drew apart, coordination became difficult, and the engagement was usually settled within a few hours.
people: 這場戰爭留下的人名極少，任何一份戰役目錄都只能列出輪廓。亞述方面，可對上年代的是中亞述王表上的君主：Apil-Eshin（約前1150–前1114年在位）、Ashur-bel-kala（約前1114–前1113年在位），以及在亞述西進中扮演主導角色的 Tiglat-Pileser I（約前1114–前1076年在位）；後者的銘文提到他率軍越過幼發拉底、進抵阿馬爾，並以「抵海之地」描述西行的目標，迪亞烏希之戰是否就落在這條路線上，無法證實。埃及方面，那一朝的法老名與最高祭司的名字都存在缺環：王朝末期諸王（拉美西斯十世、十一世一系）留下的紀年極不完整，亞蒙神最高祭司 Herihor 的紀年石刻要到其後數十年才出現，因此戰爭的直接指揮者無從指名。真正能把兩國釘在同一時空的，是更早一代的交往者：阿馬爾納書信中的亞述王 Ashur-uballit I 與其子 Abdi-Milkuti，以及米坦尼王 Tushratta 的來信；他們留下書信往還、貢賦清單與互相威脅的辭句，是十四世紀那條線索的實物支點，也讓後人知道前1118年前後的埃及與亞述彼此知道對方的名字、國號與大致方位。另一類人物只以群體出現：抄寫楔形文字敘事文本的書吏、抄錄王室年表的祭司，以及被雇來作戰的沙漠民兵與努比亞弓手。他們的名字不進王表，卻決定了戰場上真正的樣子——兵是誰的、箭從哪裡來、糧食能撐多久。
peopleEn: Very few names survive from this war, and any list of the engagement can give only an outline. On the Assyrian side the figures that can be aligned with the date are the rulers of the Middle Assyrian king list: Apil-Eshin, who reigned about 1150 to 1114 BC, Ashur-bel-kala, about 1114 to 1113 BC, and Tiglat-Pileser I, about 1114 to 1076 BC, the man who drove the westward expansion of Assyria; the inscriptions of the latter record armies crossing the Euphrates and reaching the Amurru, and describe the western objective as the land that borders the sea, but whether Dium Ush lay on that line cannot be demonstrated. On the Egyptian side there are gaps in the very names: the kings of the end of the dynasty, the line of Ramesses X and Ramesses XI, have left an extremely incomplete chronology, and the dated stela of the High Priest of Amun Herihor only appears a generation or two later, so the commander of the war cannot be named. What really pins the two countries to the same stretch of time is the generation of contacts before it: the Assyrian king Ashur-uballit I and his son Abdi-Milkuti of the Amarna letters, and the envoys of the Mitanni king Tushratta. Their correspondence, their lists of tribute and their mutually threatening phrases are the physical anchor for the fourteenth-century line of evidence, and they are what lets us know that around 1118 BC Egypt and Assyria knew each other's names, titles and general bearings. A second class of figures appears only in groups: the scribes who copied the cuneiform narrative text, the temple chroniclers who copied the royal annals, and the desert levies and Nubian archers who were hired to fight. Their names never entered the king list, yet they determined what the battlefield actually looked like, whose men the soldiers were, where the arrows came from, and how long the food would hold out.
kits: 卡面上這件埃及長矛，是早王朝時期就有的直刃長矛：銅或青銅矛頭以榫口或縛紮固定在木杆上，杆長及肩，埃及人先用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。到了第二中間期，這件兵器並沒有被淘汰，反而因為埃及的正規重裝兵源枯竭，成為僱傭步兵與徵召民兵最省事的主兵器。埃及一方的裝備大致是這樣的組合：長矛手列在前面成排，肩並肩舉矛，替後面的弓手擋住飛矢；弓是複合弓，竹木為身，角或獸皮為飾，箭鏃用銅、骨或石；盾為圓形，木胎蒙皮，尺寸比新王國時代縮小；斧與短刀用於貼身，銅柄直刃的科普什式彎刀已退居儀仗；新王國時代的雙輪輕戰車到這時更多是儀式性的象徵，實戰靠的是步兵與外來弓手。亞述一方的裝備則不同：長矛的矛頭多已改為鐵，箭鏃大量用鐵，這是中亞述時期最顯著的技術變化之一；弓仍是複合弓，但箭數更多；盾是木框蒙皮、可立在身前的高盾，另有青銅或鐵包邊的各式劍與匕首；亞述在這時已發展出真正重要的騎兵，馬匹用於戰術機動，戰車則是最高統帥與近衛的座駕；攻城方面有斜坡、擋牆與撞槌，但迪亞烏希之戰並未留下攻城記載。運輸與補給靠騾馬、牛車與人力，軍隊一旦離開幼發拉底河谷，水與糧食便要就地徵發，這是亞述在西邊作戰最吃力的環節；埃及的遠征軍同樣如此，其糧道要跨過西奈或走海路，這條遙遠的補給線本身就是埃及最脆弱的地方。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card is a straight-bladed weapon that already existed in the Early Dynastic period: a copper or bronze head fixed to a wooden shaft by socket or lashing, the shaft reaching to the shoulder, used at first to hold city walls and later to win back lost ground. By the Second Intermediate Period the weapon had not been superseded; on the contrary, because Egypt's supply of trained heavy infantry had dried up, it became the most economical main arm for mercenary foot and hastily levied militia. The Egyptian equipment on the field was something like this combination: rows of spearmen in front, standing shoulder to shoulder with their spears raised, screening the archers behind them from stray arrows; the bow was a composite bow of wood with horn or hide fittings, its arrowheads of copper, bone or stone; the shield was round, a wooden boss covered with hide, smaller than in the New Kingdom; axes and short knives served at close quarters, while the copper-hilted straight-edged khopesh had been demoted to pageantry; the light two-wheeled chariot of the New Kingdom had become largely a ceremonial symbol, and fighting was done by infantry and by imported archers. The Assyrian equipment was different: the heads of the long spears were increasingly iron, and iron was used in bulk for arrowheads, which is one of the most conspicuous technical changes of the Middle Assyrian period. The bow was still composite, but the volume of arrows was greater; the shield was a tall wooden frame covered in hide that could be set on the ground in front of the man; and there were swords and daggers edged in bronze or iron. Assyria had by this time developed a cavalry that really mattered, horses being used for tactical manoeuvre, while the chariot remained the mount of the high commander and of his guard. For siege work there were ramps, outworks and battering rams, but no siege is recorded at Dium Ush. Transport and supply rested on mules, ox carts and human porters; once an army left the Euphrates valley, water and grain had to be taken from the country it marched through, which was the most expensive link in Assyrian campaigning in the west. The Egyptian expeditionary force was in the same case, with its supply line crossing the Sinai or running by sea, and that long thin line of supply was itself Egypt's weakest point.
tactics: 中亞述時期的野戰可以從兩方面推想。亞述方面的做法，是把弓手與輕裝步兵集中成一個作戰核心，用車隊與騎兵在兩翼製造壓力，弓手的作用不是消滅敵人，而是壓制敵陣的展開，迫使其在不利的位置上接戰；一旦敵陣出現缺口，國王與近衛便帶著車隊一次衝入，不給對方重新整隊的時間。埃及方面的傳統做法承襲新王國的經驗：長矛手在前列成密集盾牆，弓手在後或兩翼成排射擊，以齊射製造壓力，直到敵人衝到矛尖可及的距離才讓開；步兵之間靠號角與旗幟保持同步，隊形一旦鬆動便難以重整，這也說明埃及的密集矛陣一旦被切開就會連鎖崩潰。就地形處理而言，敘事文本把交鋒放在城外開闊地，雙方都不急著進逼城池，符合中亞述時期亞述作戰「野戰求決、攻城另計」的習慣：野戰勝負一次決定，攻城則是另一場耗費巨大的工程。補給是第二個關鍵：埃及的軍隊離開尼羅河谷之後完全依賴就地徵發，亞述的軍隊依賴幼發拉底中游的城市與驛站網，兩者在作戰半徑上的差異，實際上決定了誰能長期留在前線、誰必須在補給耗盡之前退走。季節也值得一提：埃及的征戰季通常在氾濫之後的夏秋，即以埃曆第四至第六月、合公曆約七至九月；敘事文本並未保留月份，本目錄所填的月份是按此作戰季節推填，不代表文獻記載。
tacticsEn: The conduct of a field battle in the Middle Assyrian period can be reconstructed from two sides. The Assyrian method was to concentrate archers and light infantry into a single body of combat, to bring pressure on both flanks with the chariot corps and the cavalry, and to use the archers not to destroy the enemy but to deny him the chance to deploy, forcing him to accept contact on ground of the Assyrians' choosing. The moment a gap appeared in the opposing line, the king and his guard would ride in with the chariots in a single stroke, giving the enemy no time to reform. The Egyptian practice of the period followed the lessons of the New Kingdom: spearmen in the front rank formed a dense shield wall, archers behind and on the flanks fired in volleys, and the volleys kept up the pressure until the enemy was close enough to be reached by the point of the spear, at which moment the front rank would open a gap. Synchronisation between the foot was kept by horn and by standard, and once a formation loosened it could not easily be re-established, which is also why a dense Egyptian spear line, once cut, came apart in a chain reaction. As for the ground, the narrative text places the encounter in open country outside the town, and neither side presses at once toward the walls, which fits the Middle Assyrian habit of seeking decision in the open field and treating siege as a separate and far more costly undertaking. Supply was the second key. An Egyptian army once it had left the Nile valley depended entirely on requisition, while an Assyrian army depended on the cities and relay stations of the middle Euphrates; the difference in the radius each could sustain in the field decided, in practice, who could stay in the front line and who had to withdraw before the food ran out. The season matters as well: Egyptian campaigning usually fell in the summer and autumn after the inundation, that is the fourth to sixth months of the Egyptian calendar, roughly July to September in the Julian year. The narrative text preserves no month, and the month entered in this record follows that campaigning season; it does not represent anything the sources state.
data: 可以核對的數字分三類。第一類是年表：中文的戰爭列表把此役繫於公元前1118年，學界一般只肯把相關事件放在公元前十二世紀末至前十一世紀初；中亞述王表可對照的君主在位年數，Apil-Eshin 約前1150–前1114年、Ashur-bel-kala 約前1114–前1113年、Tiglat-Pileser I 約前1114–前1076年。埃及方面，拉美西斯十世與十一世一系的在位年代本身就有爭議，學者常把拉美西斯王朝末段至 Herihor 掌權之間的一段稱作「弱法老的時代」，年分約前1120–前1070年，迪亞烏希的戰事若屬這一段，時間框架是相容的。第二類是距離與地理：亞述首都到巴比倫約三百五十公里，到幼發拉底中游城鎮約五百公里，到阿馬爾諸城約六百至七百公里；埃及的西奈陸路到迦南約七百至九百公里，經比布洛斯走海路到埃及約二千公里；這些數字說明「亞述打到埃及門口」在地理上做得到，但代價極高。第三類是物質與考古：Tell Brak、Zincirli、Arslan Tash 等中亞述時期遺址出土大量馬匹骨骼與車具殘件，顯示騎兵與車隊規模不小；同一時期亞述的鐵器數量急增，箭鏃與刀劍成組出土，是中亞述軍事技術最硬的證據。兵力人數則無從核實：亞述王室銘文慣用「無數」「全境之兵」一類修辭，埃及方面的編年殘缺，因此雙方出動人數只能說在數千至數萬的量級，沒有任何一份可靠文獻給出具體數字，任何寫下「雙方各出十萬人」的說法都應當打折扣看待。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is the chronology: the Chinese list of battles ties this engagement to 1118 BC, while scholarship will only place the related event in the late twelfth or the early eleventh century BC. The reigns of the Middle Assyrian rulers that can be compared are Apil-Eshin, about 1150 to 1114 BC, Ashur-bel-kala, about 1114 to 1113 BC, and Tiglat-Pileser I, about 1114 to 1076 BC. On the Egyptian side the dates of the kings of the line of Ramesses X and Ramesses XI are themselves disputed; scholars commonly call the stretch between the end of the Ramesside dynasty and the accession of Herihor the era of the weak pharaohs, dated about 1120 to 1070 BC, and if the fighting at Dium Ush belongs to that stretch the chronology is compatible. The second class is distance and geography: from the Assyrian capital to Babylon is about three hundred and fifty kilometres, to the middle Euphrates towns about five hundred, and to the cities of the Amurru about six to seven hundred; from Egypt the land route across Sinai to Canaan is seven to nine hundred kilometres, while the sea route through Byblos to Egypt is about two thousand. These figures show that Assyria could physically reach Egypt's doorstep, and also how costly the attempt would have been. The third class is material and archaeological: Tell Brak, Zincirli and Arslan Tash have yielded large quantities of horse bone and vehicle fittings from the Middle Assyrian period, showing that neither cavalry nor chariot corps were small, and the sharp rise in Assyrian iron in the same period, with arrowheads and blades found in groups, is the hardest evidence for Middle Assyrian military technology. Numbers of men cannot be checked at all: Assyrian royal inscriptions habitually use formulas such as countless and the troops of the whole land, and the Egyptian chronicle is fragmentary, so the forces on both sides can only be said to lie in the range of thousands to tens of thousands. No reliable document gives a figure, and any statement that ten thousand men a side took part should be treated with a heavy discount.
cause: 打起來的背景有四層。最遠的一層是國際格局的崩塌：公元前十三世紀末至前十二世紀初，赫梯帝國崩解，塞納河流域出現權力真空，阿馬爾諸城像被遺下的空屋；與此同時，「海上民族」的衝擊震盪整個東地中海，迦南海岸的城邦一個接一個衰亡。亞述正是在這個真空裡迅速西進，把阿馬爾與幼發拉底上游收進勢力範圍。第二層是埃及自身的崩解：新王國在阿馬爾納危機之後從未真正恢復對迦南的統治；到了拉美西斯王朝末年，內部已是王權空心化，法老缺錢、缺兵、缺可信的將領，軍隊靠僱傭兵與努比亞弓手拼湊，對外只剩下守。第三層是爭奪物的具體形態：迪亞烏希之戰若確實發生在敘利亞北部，說明爭的是迦南這條連接安納托利亞、黎凡特與埃及的走廊，誰控制得了它，誰就控制得了東地中海的商路與穀物。第四層是領導層的分裂：埃及在第二中間期出現三角洲與上游兩套權力中心，彼此不能統合；亞述的王權雖集中，卻正處於擴張的消耗期，國王更有可能用一次遠征來穩住自己的地位，而不是主動避戰。直接導火線的記載沒有留下；比較合理的推測是亞述軍隊向西南推進、逼近埃及的邊界或商路，埃及於是派出由步兵、弓手與雇傭兵拼成的遠征混合部隊迎戰，雙方在迪亞烏希城外狹路相逢。
causeEn: The background to the fighting has four layers. The most distant is the collapse of the international order: from the late thirteenth to the early twelfth century BC the Hittite empire fell apart, a power vacuum opened in the upper Euphrates, and the cities of the Amurru lay about like empty houses; at the same time the shock of the Sea Peoples disturbed the whole eastern Mediterranean and the coastal cities of Canaan declined one after another. It was precisely into that vacuum that Assyria moved quickly west, drawing the Amurru and the upper Euphrates into its sphere. The second layer is Egypt's own breakdown. After the Amarna crisis the New Kingdom never truly regained its hold on Canaan; by the end of the Ramesside dynasty the monarchy was hollow, the pharaoh short of money, short of soldiers and short of commanders he could trust, the army pieced together from mercenaries and Nubian archers, and all that remained was defence. The third layer is the concrete shape of what was at stake: if the battle at Dium Ush did indeed take place in northern Syria, then the prize was the corridor of Canaan linking Anatolia, the Levant and Egypt, and control of that corridor meant control of the trade and the grain of the eastern Mediterranean. The fourth layer is the division of the leadership: Egypt of the Second Intermediate Period had two centres of power, the Delta and the upper river, which could not be integrated, while the Assyrian kingship, though concentrated, was in the consuming phase of expansion, and a king at that moment was more likely to steady his position with a distant campaign than to avoid contact. No record of the immediate occasion survives. The most reasonable reconstruction is that an Assyrian army pushed south-west toward the Egyptian frontier or the Egyptian trade routes, and that Egypt sent out a mixed expedition of infantry, archers and mercenaries to meet it, the two sides running into each other in the open outside Dium Ush.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接後果無從詳細重建，但它在幾條線上留下可追的痕跡。第一，亞述西進的節奏：迪亞烏希之後不到一百年，亞述在阿馬爾的統治已鞏固，隨後在帝國時代把整個黎凡特納入版圖；中亞述時期的每一次試探，都在為後來的亞述帝國鋪路。可以說，迪亞烏希是亞述第一次真正試探到埃及防線的一役，之後亞述把重心轉回北方與東方，而在埃及方向長期維持壓力，直到新亞述王朝才有條件重新挑戰。第二，埃及的方向：這場戰鬥之後，埃及在迦南的殘餘影響力迅速收縮，注意力全部轉向南方與三角洲，第十八王朝式的帝國結構再也沒有恢復，取而代之的是第二十王朝末期的分崩與第二十一王朝的割據；直到第二十五王朝的塞沙爾特時代，非洲的軍力才重新壓過北方。第三，史料上的意義：這場戰爭幾乎沒有留下任何一方的官方紀錄，卻在楔形文字的敘事文獻裡留下一段可讀的文字，這是研究者在阿馬爾納書信之後、亞述帝國之前，能拿到的少數直接涉及兩國交鋒的材料之一。第四，對「海上民族」年代的重新解讀：過去學界把前十二世紀上半葉視為埃及最衰弱的時期，近年的文本研究則顯示，埃及仍具備派出遠征混合部隊、在迦南作戰的能力，中間只是缺少留下紀錄的制度與文書傳統。
impactEn: The direct consequences of the war cannot be reconstructed in detail, but it left traceable marks along several lines. The first is the tempo of the Assyrian advance. Within a century of Dium Ush the Assyrian hold over the Amurru was secure, and the empire that followed drew the whole Levant into its orbit; every probing expedition of the Middle Assyrian period was paving the road for the later Assyrian empire. Dium Ush, one can say, was the first time Assyria really tested the Egyptian defensive line, and afterwards Assyria turned its weight back to the north and the east while keeping up steady pressure in the Egyptian direction, until the Neo-Assyrian dynasty was in a position to challenge Egypt again. The second is Egypt's own direction. After this clash the last shreds of Egyptian influence in Canaan contracted rapidly and Egyptian attention turned wholly southward and toward the Delta; the imperial structure of the Eighteenth Dynasty was never restored, and was replaced by the fragmentation of the end of the Twentieth Dynasty and the divided sovereignty of the Twenty-First. Not until the Twenty-Fifth Dynasty and the age of the Kushite kings did the military weight of Africa once again outweigh the north. The third is the significance of the evidence. The war left almost no official record on either side, yet it survives in a readable stretch of cuneiform narrative text, and this is one of the few materials directly touching a clash between the two countries that a researcher can pick up in the long gap between the Amarna letters and the Assyrian empire. The fourth is the reinterpretation of the age of the Sea Peoples. Older scholarship treated the first half of the twelfth century BC as the point of Egypt's greatest weakness, whereas recent textual work shows that Egypt still had the capacity to send out mixed expeditions and fight in Canaan; what it lacked in the interval was the institutions and the documentary habit that would have written the outcome down.
result: 勝負本身無從確定，這必須先講清楚。現存的楔形文字敘事文本流傳殘缺，抄本年代也遠晚於事件；亞述一方的王室碑刻裡查不到這場戰役的記載，埃及方面同一時期的編年又幾乎空白，因此「誰勝誰負」只能從形勢推敲。就形勢而言，最合理的讀法是：交鋒沒有為埃及帶來任何迦南土地，亞述也沒有把戰線推進到尼羅河谷，雙方在消耗之後各自收手，隨後亞述在數十年內消化阿馬爾，埃及則把國策整體轉向南方與三角洲。至於這段文字為何值得記錄並流傳，合理的解釋有兩種：一是編纂者把這次遭遇當作王權合法性的素材，用以說明王的守護；二是這段文字在亞述本土並非主流傳統，卻在其他傳承中保存下來，成為後世重新發現此役的唯一線索。無論取哪一種解釋，結果的指向是清楚的：迪亞烏希沒有改變任何一方的版圖，卻是亞述西進與埃及退縮這兩條長期曲線的交點，標誌著埃及在迦南的帝國時代正式落幕。
resultEn: The outcome cannot be established, and that has to be said first. The cuneiform narrative text that survives is fragmentary, and its copies are far later than the event; there is no mention of the war in the royal inscriptions of Assyria, and the Egyptian chronicle for the same stretch is almost blank, so the question of who won can only be reasoned from the situation. Read that way, the most likely reading is that the encounter brought Egypt no land in Canaan, that Assyria did not carry the war to the Nile valley either, and that after the drain of the fighting both sides withdrew, Assyria then digesting the Amurru over the following decades while Egypt turned its whole policy southward and toward the Delta. As for why the text was worth recording and why it was transmitted, there are two reasonable explanations: either the compiler took the encounter as material for the legitimacy of kingship, to show the protection of the king, or the text was not part of the mainstream Assyrian tradition but was preserved in another line of transmission, and so became the only clue by which the battle was later rediscovered. On either explanation the direction of the result is plain: Dium Ush changed no one's territory, but it is the point at which the two long curves, the Assyrian advance to the west and the Egyptian withdrawal, cross, and it marks the formal end of Egypt's imperial age in Canaan.
